case.pattern_description: This undocumented fraud pattern involves a fan-in spike where several unrelated customer cards suddenly made online purchases paying a single recipient email domain, sc.rr.com. The activity directly impacts customer C01727 on visa debit card C01727-K2, along with 16 connected cards across multiple accounts. The pattern was detected following an analyst request to investigate transaction 3660263 and uncover related card activity, which triggered the detector fanin_r_emaildomain_k3_1d_r0p2 after four cards paid the recipient domain in a single day.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report concerns unauthorized activity conducted on visa debit card C01727-K2 belonging to customer C01727 under case id HHF-006. Between 2017-01-17 and 2017-01-28, an unauthorized party executed three online transactions totaling 967.68 dollars without any associated device identifiers. The activity commenced with transaction 3660261 on 2017-01-17 at 15:29 for 305.41 dollars, followed by transaction 3660262 on 2017-01-18 at 19:40 for 366.35 dollars. A third transaction, 3660263, was carried out on 2017-01-28 at 07:59:42 for 295.92 dollars. All three transactions were conducted online under product code C within billing region 231. The unauthorized transactions were carried out as purchases paying one recipient email domain, sc.rr.com, that suddenly drew payments from several unrelated customers' cards. The shared recipient email domain sc.rr.com connected card C01727-K2 to other cards including C00534-K2, C01357-K1, C01507-K1, C01594-K1, C02167-K2, C03060-K1, C04146-K1, and C04668-K1. The activity is suspicious because the pattern matches none of the documented fraud typologies and card C01727-K2 has prior confirmed-fraud cases including CC-0723, CC-1833, and CC-1501. The cardholder has not yet been contacted. Bank containment and response actions included blocking the card, creating a case, monitoring connected cards, escalating to an analyst, and filing this report.
